name: Versys Site Health Toolkit
author: Versys Media

sections.description:
Versys Site Health Toolkit gives administrators one clear dashboard for checking the technical condition of a WordPress website.

It combines actionable diagnostics, installed component requirements, safe maintenance actions and a redacted support report without requiring an account or sending telemetry to an external service.

Versys Site Health Toolkit is developed and maintained by Versys Media, a digital agency specialising in WordPress development, website maintenance and technical support.

Health and compatibility checks

  • WordPress core version and pending updates
  • PHP version and recommended PHP extensions
  • WordPress memory allowance
  • HTTPS consistency and HTTP references in published content
  • REST API and front-end loopback availability
  • Approximate server-side front-end response time
  • WordPress cron status and overdue events
  • Upload-directory access
  • Autoloaded database option size
  • Active theme WordPress and PHP requirements
  • Installed plugin WordPress and PHP requirements
  • Plugin and theme updates
  • Plugin active and inactive state
  • Permalink configuration
  • Environment-aware debug configuration
  • Search engine visibility
  • Dashboard plugin and theme editor exposure
  • Elementor availability when Elementor is installed
  • MySQL or MariaDB compatibility
  • Total database footprint
  • Inactive plugin and theme footprint
  • Persistent object-cache detection

Practical tools

  • Run a fresh scan and compare the score with the previous scan
  • Review every installed plugin, including inactive plugins
  • Download a timestamped plain-text support report
  • Copy a concise health summary for support requests
  • Search and filter the installed-plugin compatibility matrix
  • Refresh permalink rules
  • Remove expired WordPress transients
  • Flush the WordPress object cache
  • Regenerate Elementor generated assets when Elementor is active
  • Review a local audit trail of maintenance actions

Privacy

The plugin does not collect telemetry, create an external account, place tracking code on the public website or send site information to Versys Media.

The REST API and loopback diagnostics request only URLs belonging to the same WordPress installation. Scans, score history and maintenance logs remain inside the site’s own WordPress database.

Compatibility results are indicators rather than guarantees. Create a current backup and test significant changes on a staging site.

sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or install it from the WordPress Plugin Directory.
  2. Activate Versys Site Health Toolkit.
  3. Open Tools > Versys Health in the WordPress administration menu.
  4. Review the results before running any optional maintenance action.

Only administrators with the manage_options capability can view the dashboard, run maintenance tools or download reports.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin change my content during a scan?

No. Diagnostics are read-only. They do not edit posts, pages, media, users, themes, plugins or site settings.

What do the maintenance tools change?

Each tool performs only the action named on its button. The plugin can refresh rewrite rules, remove expired transients, flush the object cache and, when Elementor is active, clear Elementor’s generated assets. These actions run only after an administrator deliberately selects them.

Does this replace WordPress Site Health?

No. It complements WordPress Site Health with a different dashboard, an installed-plugin compatibility matrix, score comparison, maintenance tools and a shareable redacted report.

Does a healthy result guarantee compatibility?

No. The plugin checks the environment and the requirements declared by installed components. A complex theme or plugin conflict may still require staging tests and developer review.

Does it send data to Versys Media?

No. There is no telemetry, remote account, tracking pixel or external analytics connection.

What is stored in the database?

The plugin stores a short local maintenance log, up to 12 compact scan-history entries and a temporary five-minute scan cache. Uninstalling the plugin removes this data.

  • Added developer information to the public plugin description.

1.1.2

  • Moved the dashboard under the standard WordPress Tools menu following directory review feedback.

1.1.1

  • Removed the optional Plugin URI header to keep it distinct from the Author URI for WordPress.org submission.

  • Rebuilt the dashboard banner with a navy, royal blue and cyan visual system.
  • Added server-side front-end response timing.
  • Added database footprint monitoring with a conservative review threshold.
  • Added inactive plugin and theme footprint checks.
  • Added persistent object-cache detection to the system snapshot and reports.
  • Added a one-click copyable support summary.
  • Added instant search for the installed-plugin compatibility matrix.

  • Changed the primary interface accent to Versys blue.
  • Reserved red styling for critical and failed health states.

  • Initial public release.
  • Added local health and compatibility diagnostics.
  • Added PHP extension, autoloaded option, search visibility and code editor checks.
  • Added active theme requirement checks.
  • Added an all-installed-plugin compatibility matrix with active and inactive states.
  • Added scan score comparisons and compact local history.
  • Added safe maintenance tools and a local audit trail.
  • Added timestamped redacted support reports.
